what_it_does: The model's score for a sentence is the sum of its probabilities for these grades (2 planned, 3 committed): loose first, tightened by the floors.

The starting gate: an asset's question goes to a sentence only when the sentence scores at least this against the asset's search phrases, until the skip rule (skip.max_loss) has fitted the asset's own gate from graded sentences. 0 asks every asset of every sentence.
how_to_tune: A starting value only; the fitted gate replaces it.

what_it_does: A sentence has an asset when the posterior for its best asset reaches this (level unit), or when the decayed sum below does (level paragraph).
how_to_tune: Tested 2026-10-22 with decay 0.4: 0.3 best. Raise it if sentences get the wrong asset; lower it if too many get none.

what_it_does: A sentence whose own best asset is under the floor adds up, for each asset, its own score and every earlier sentence's in its paragraph, each multiplied by this per sentence back (one back x0.4, two back x0.16); the asset with the highest sum takes it at the floor. 0 turns the rule off.
how_to_tune: Tested on the graded sentences 2026-10-22: 0.4 best of 0 to 1.

what_it_does: The starting gate: a sentence goes to a measure's question when its best similarity to the measure's phrases and definition reaches this, or a word pattern matches, until the skip rule (skip.max_loss) has fitted the measure's own gate from graded sentences.
how_to_tune: A starting value only; the fitted gate replaces it. The feedback rounds find what the gate misses.

what_it_does: Also send the measure's best N sentences by similarity, whatever their score. 0 = off.

The skip rule: each label's gate is the highest cosine that loses at most this share of the sentences a person graded yes under the current question (at their design weights); word-pattern matches are always asked. Fitted by ./wbg check <set> --evaluate, read by the next run.
A label needs at least this many graded yes before its gate is fitted; until then the starting gate above applies.

After each model answer, combine the model's score with how similar the sentence is to the sentences a person graded for the same label (src/posterior.py). Off = the model's score alone.
